messages:
Samir (CSE): Quick weekly check-in for Harbor's private VPC — rolling up region-by-region health and a few KMS notes. TL;DR: overall uptime good, a couple of short KMS spikes in eu-west, small increase in token spend from batch jobs.

Leah (Eng): Thanks Samir. Sharing the quick numbers we saw this week:
- us-east-1: uptime 99.98%, p95 latency 120ms, 0.4% error rate
- eu-west-1: uptime 99.85%, p95 latency 160ms, 1.2% error rate (errors clustered around 2026-03-12 03:10-03:25 UTC)
- ap-south-1: uptime 99.95%, p95 latency 210ms, 0.6% error rate
Spend: ~+18% week-over-week driven by nightly bulk-embed jobs.

Marco (Infra): Noted on eu-west errors. We correlated those with short periods of KMS latency — KMS calls to customer-managed HSM had multi-second tails. Stack snippet from the logs:```
2026-03-12T03:11:07Z WARN kms-client: request latency 2400ms (retrying)
2026-03-12T03:11:12Z ERROR serve: request failed: context deadline exceeded
```
Root cause looks like a transient HSM maintenance window + small network jitter on the customer's gateway. No kernel panics or infra restarts.

Rosa (Harbor): We saw about ~12 failed inference calls in our dashboard during that window, caused visible timeouts for some users. Harbor's infra team confirms there was an HSM firmware patch on their end at 03:00 UTC. They didn't think it would affect service but acknowledged it could cause occasional elevated latencies.

Samir (CSE): OK — action items: (1) Marco / Infra to add an automated soft-fallback to Redwood-managed KMS for short HSM unavailability windows (config toggle per-account); (2) Ask Harbor if patch windows can be scheduled with a 2-hour notice + maintenance flag so we can route; (3) Leah to monitor the increased embed job spend and suggest batching tweaks or token limits.

Leah (Eng): For spend: recommend throttling bulk-embed jobs to 50 rps and enabling prefix caching for repeated doc prefixes. I can send a config snippet to Harbor:```
batch_config:
  target_rps: 50
  cache_prefix: true
```
This should cut the spike by ~40% without affecting daily throughput.

Marco (Infra): I'll prototype a fallback policy and flag it as opt-in for the account. Rough plan: detect KMS latency > 800ms for 3 consecutive calls -> switch to managed-KMS routing for 10min, emit incident. Will post PR tomorrow.

Rosa (Harbor): That fallback option sounds fine. On scheduling — Harbor can provide a calendar invite for major maintenance. They asked if Redwood can surface a maintenance window header so Harbor's ops can mark calls as lower priority during patching.

Samir (CSE): Good ask — Leah, can we add a custom header passthrough that Harbor sets (x-harbor-maintenance: true) and we deprioritize non-critical inference? If yes, we can include in the enablement doc.

Leah (Eng): Yep, doable. We'll also add a short runbook for the Harbor engs: how to toggle the header, how to opt into managed-KMS fallback, and recommended embed batch settings. I'll draft and share by EOD Friday.

incident-bot: Created incident INC-20260312-74 for KMS latency spike in eu-west-1 (severity: low). Assigned to Marco.

Samir (CSE): Closing notes: renewal health — still green but monitorable risk due to multiple short-daytime timeouts. If we get another 2 similar spikes this quarter, I'll flag for renewal outreach. Next enablement session scheduled with Harbor for 2026-03-18 14:00 UTC to walk through fallback and batch configs. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

Rosa (Harbor): Thanks everyone — Harbor will share the maintenance calendar and confirm preference on managed-KMS fallback. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:
